old: It's built from a word for weapons plus a word meaning 'to stand still.'
Its Latin root sistere means 'to halt' — the arms simply stop moving.
French, Italian, Portuguese, and Spanish all have near-identical cousins of this word.
clues: This kind of formal agreement between nations takes its name from Latin words for weapons and for making something stand still.
It is an agreement by warring sides to stop fighting, more formal than a brief ceasefire or truce but not yet a full peace treaty.
Many countries mark November 11 as the Day named for this, recalling the end of fighting in 1918. Spanish speakers call it armisticio.
